global.headline: IRAN'S STRIKE PAUSE COLLAPSES: MISSILES HIT JORDAN, SAUDI ARABIA JOINS US STRIKES IN IRAQ, TANKERS BURN IN EGYPT
summary: The four-night lull in the Iran war ended abruptly Wednesday when Iran's Revolutionary Guard fired ballistic missiles at Jordan's Muwaffaq Salti air base, which hosts US forces, at around 1:45pm Gulf time — the first direct Iranian strike on American positions since the pause began 25 July. Jordan's military said it intercepted and downed five missiles; CENTCOM confirmed all missiles were intercepted with no casualties or damage. The same day, US and Saudi aircraft carried out joint strikes on Iran-backed Popular Mobilisation Forces militia sites across Iraq, killing at least 20 fighters and wounding 32 — the first time Riyadh has claimed responsibility for strikes inside Iraq this war. Saudi Arabia said the action was self-defence after Iran-aligned militias launched more than 30 drone attacks on its Eastern Region oil facilities over 72 hours, including a second consecutive day of strikes as this report went to press; Yemen's Houthis separately claimed a strike on Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline. Iran's IRGC said it had "struck and stopped" three tankers it accused of ignoring its warnings on an "unsafe and illegal route" through Hormuz, though no casualties or independently confirmed damage were reported. Tehran also gave its first response to Oman's Malacca-style Hormuz fee proposal (put to it 28 July): rejection, keeping the fundamental gap between Washington's demand for guaranteed free transit and Iran's demand for supervisory/toll authority unresolved.

The war's geography widened further when a drone — unclaimed, but assessed by two security sources as the likely cause — struck the floating gas-storage tanker Energos Winter at Egypt's Mediterranean port of Damietta, igniting a fire that spread to a second vessel, the Gaslog Salem; Egypt's petroleum ministry confirmed a fire at the port but did not address the drone assessment, and no injuries were reported. It is the first attack on shipping outside the Gulf/Red Sea theatre this war. Brent crude jumped roughly 6.6% to around $90 a barrel on the combined news. Separately, Benjamin Netanyahu and Volodymyr Zelensky each held their own White House meetings with Donald Trump on Tuesday, both men in Washington for the funeral of the late Senator Lindsey Graham; the White House called the roughly 90-minute Netanyahu meeting "positive and productive," focused on Iran's nuclear file, Lebanon negotiations and expanding the Abraham Accords, with no new agreement announced. Zelensky and Trump discussed US licences for Ukraine to produce its own Patriot interceptors. Inside Iran, the post-war execution surge continues unabated: a mass hunger strike by more than 1,000 death-row inmates at Ghezel Hesar Prison, begun 13 July, is now in its third week, with rights groups and video reviewed by the Guardian indicating some prisoners have sewn their lips shut in protest; Iranian judicial authorities have not responded.
global.geopolitical: A single day that ends the strike pause, draws Saudi Arabia into direct military action on Iraqi soil for the first time, and spreads the war to Egyptian shipping marks the broadest simultaneous escalation of fronts since the conflict resumed in July, even as separate Trump meetings with Netanyahu and Zelensky underline how thoroughly the Iran and Ukraine wars now share the same diplomatic calendar.
global.socioeconomic: Oil's jump back toward $90 on a widening war — now touching Iraq, Egypt and potentially the East-West pipeline as well as Hormuz — threatens to reverse the relief trade- and energy-dependent economies like Singapore's had drawn from the prior week's price falls, just as Iran's rejection of the Oman fee framework removes the clearest near-term off-ramp for the strait.

global.headline: KUMAMOTO EARTHQUAKE: MAGNITUDE REVISED TO 7.1, DEATH TOLL CLIMBS TO 18 AS RESCUERS RACE THROUGH RUBBLE
summary: Japan's Meteorological Agency revised Tuesday's Kyushu earthquake to magnitude 7.1 on its own scale (the US Geological Survey's moment-magnitude estimate remains 6.8), as the confirmed death toll climbed to 18, including a foreigner, with at least 62 injured, six seriously. Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi ordered "all available resources" mobilised in what she called a race against time; some 345 rescue teams comprising 1,139 responders from eight prefectures, plus local agencies, have been deployed, for roughly 1,410 personnel in total. The quake has produced around 190 aftershocks in the 24 hours since it struck at 4:27pm local time Tuesday, 20km south of Kumamoto City. The chimney collapse at a Nippon Paper Industries factory in Yatsushiro, initially reported with several workers unaccounted for, is now confirmed to have killed five people, while seven others were rescued from the debris. Rescue efforts continue at Kumamoto's Aeon Mall in Kashima Town, where a suspected gas leak explosion following the quake killed two women in their twenties and left others trapped.
global.geopolitical: Neighbours moved quickly with condolences and offers of help — South Korea's President Lee pledged solidarity, Taiwan's President Lai offered support, and China expressed condolences — underscoring how a major Japanese disaster still draws swift regional diplomatic response even amid broader regional tensions.
global.socioeconomic: A death toll that has grown roughly ninefold in a day, on a quake now rated stronger on Japan's own scale than first thought, points to a longer and more resource-intensive recovery for Kyushu's rebuilt commercial and industrial core than initially assumed.

global.headline: GHANA HIT BY NATIONWIDE BLACKOUT AS POWER GRID FAILS
summary: A fault on Ghana's National Interconnected Transmission System at around 3:11am Wednesday triggered the simultaneous tripping of multiple generating plants, plunging the capital Accra, the commercial hub of Kumasi and much of the country's north into darkness. Grid operator GRIDCo activated its system-restoration procedures and said engineers were working with power-sector stakeholders to bring supply back online, while launching a technical investigation into the disturbance's precise cause. Ghana Water Limited apologised to customers for a nationwide disruption to water supply after the outage forced the shutdown of its treatment plants and pumping stations.
global.socioeconomic: A grid-wide failure that knocks out both power and water simultaneously across the capital and commercial hub exposes how thin Ghana's margin for a single-point transmission fault remains, with knock-on costs for businesses, hospitals and households until GRIDCo confirms the root cause and full restoration.

global.headline: THREE FIREFIGHTERS KILLED BATTLING GREEK WILDFIRES AS FRANCE BRACES FOR A FRESH FLARE-UP
summary: Two Greek firefighters died on Crete on Wednesday after becoming trapped in their vehicle while moving between fire fronts battling a wind-driven blaze in the island's Rethymno region, a popular tourist area; residents of three nearby villages, including Krya Vrysi, were ordered to evacuate. A third firefighter died in a separate blaze in the Peloponnese the same day. Meanwhile the wildfire west of Bordeaux — at one point four times the size of Paris — and Madrid's fire have both been contained for now, officials in France and Spain said, but authorities warned the French blaze could surge again as a fresh heatwave and strong winds move in. The EU's emergency response chief warned that Greece and Italy face a heightened wildfire risk in the coming weeks.
global.geopolitical: Three firefighter deaths in a single day, arriving just as France and Spain's fires show tentative signs of containment, keeps pressure on the EU's cross-border firefighting-resource-sharing arrangements and its broader climate-adaptation push.
global.socioeconomic: A summer that has already produced record-scale fires in Spain and mass evacuations in France now adds fresh fatalities and a fragile containment in two more countries, compounding tourism and agricultural losses across southern Europe as the season's risk window stays open.

global.headline: SALMAN RUSHDIE'S ATTACKER CONVICTED OF FEDERAL TERRORISM CHARGES
summary: A federal jury found Hadi Matar, 28, guilty on all charges, including engaging in an act of transnational terrorism, over his August 2022 stabbing of author Salman Rushdie on stage in western New York. Matar is already serving a 25-year New York state sentence for attempted murder; the new federal conviction carries a potential life sentence. Rushdie was slashed 15 times in the attack, losing the sight in one eye.
global.geopolitical: A federal terrorism conviction, on top of an existing state sentence, sets a marker for how US courts treat ideologically motivated attacks on writers and free-expression figures, with implications for how similar cases are prosecuted going forward.

singapore.headline: GOVERNMENT UNVEILS S$900 MILLION SUPPORT PACKAGE AS MIDDLE EAST ESCALATION THREATENS TO PUSH UP COSTS
summary: Acting Transport Minister and Second Minister for Finance Jeffrey Siow delivered a ministerial statement on the impact of the Middle East situation on Singapore, announcing a second support package worth around S$900 million. Every Singaporean household will receive an additional S$300 in CDC vouchers in January 2027; about 15,200 hawkers and market stallholders will get up to S$1,200 each in rental support from September; and monthly ComCare Interim Assistance payouts rise to at least S$250 for up to three months, with more for households with greater needs or more dependents, alongside more flexible eligibility. Siow said global energy prices are expected to stay elevated as the war continues, pushing up costs for petrol, diesel, electricity and some imported goods. The new package brings total government support announced since the war's outbreak to roughly S$2 billion, on top of the S$1 billion package unveiled in April and measures already in Budget 2026.
singapore.geopolitical: A second cost-of-living package explicitly tied to the Middle East war — arriving on the same day the conflict widened into Iraq and Egypt — shows how directly Singapore's domestic budget calculus now tracks the war's trajectory nine-plus months in.
singapore.socioeconomic: Doubling total war-related support to roughly S$2 billion in under four months signals the government sees no near-term relief on energy costs, with targeted help for hawkers and lower-income households aimed at cushioning the sharpest edges of imported inflation.

singapore.headline: DOMESTIC WORKER SENTENCED TO LIFE FOR SMOTHERING EMPLOYER'S FATHER, 73, WITH A PILLOW
summary: Sumiyati, a 53-year-old Indonesian domestic worker, was convicted of murder and sentenced to life imprisonment on Wednesday over the 2022 killing of her employer's father in a Bishan Street 23 flat. The court heard she was angered by his accusation that she had stolen his wife's jewellery; she waited until she heard him snoring, then pressed a pillow over his face for around 30 minutes until he stopped struggling, before taking his wallet and mobile phone and packing her belongings to leave. She was arrested shortly after midnight on 29 April 2022, hours after the victim's wife returned home and discovered him dead.
singapore.socioeconomic: A rare domestic-worker murder conviction reaching a life sentence renews scrutiny of employer-worker relationship strains and dispute-resolution channels in Singapore's foreign domestic worker system.

singapore.headline: FOUR CHARGED OVER MODIFIED FOODPANDA APP THAT LET FOREIGNERS WORK DELIVERY JOBS ILLEGALLY
summary: Four men aged 28 to 45 were charged after police, acting on a Ministry of Manpower tip-off, said they had provided a modified Foodpanda app enabling foreigners to take on delivery jobs illegally. The modified app let users bypass the platform's real-time selfie verification by uploading a static photo of the legitimate account holder instead, allowing unauthorised foreign users to impersonate account owners and operate on accounts that were not theirs; those users paid between S$50 and S$120 a week for access. The four face charges of access with intent to commit cheating under the Computer Misuse Act and the Penal Code.
singapore.socioeconomic: The scheme's weekly-fee structure points to an organised, ongoing market for circumventing gig-platform verification controls, adding to Singapore's broader enforcement challenge around illegal foreign labour in the platform economy.

word.definition: Literally, designed or used to cause fire (as of a bomb, device or attack); more broadly, tending to stir up conflict, anger or violence.
word.etymology: From Latin "incendiarius," from "incendium" (a fire, conflagration) and the verb "incendere" ("to set alight, to kindle" — from in- + candere, "to glow or shine white-hot"). English adopted the word in both the literal and figurative senses by the 16th century.
word.example: Whether it was the drone that set two gas tankers ablaze in Egypt, the wildfires killing firefighters on Crete, or the missiles that ended Iran's four-night pause, Wednesday's news was incendiary in every sense of the word.
